stem.text: Use the alternating series test to determine whether the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{\left(-1\right)^{n + 1}}{\sqrt{n} + 2} \), converges or diverges. Verify the conditions of the test.

answer_key.label: The series converges by the alternating series test, because \( |a_n| \) decreases to 0.

worked_solution.text: The factor \( (-1)^{n+1} \) makes the terms alternate, so the alternating series test applies once its two conditions hold.
The sizes \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{n} + 2} \) decrease because the denominator increases with n.
The terms alternate, their sizes decrease, and the sizes approach 0, so \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \) converges by the alternating series test.

options.label: The series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series test named for a series whose terms are not all positive, its hypothesis never checked

options.label: The series converges by the alternating series test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} |a_n| = 0 \).
options.derivation: the alternating series test applied with only the limit condition stated, the decrease left out

options.label: The series converges by the alternating series test, because \( |a_n| \) decreases to 0.
The series converges by the nth term test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0 \).
options.derivation: convergence concluded from the terms approaching 0 alone, the alternation never used
